purpose: Registered before any trial of the held-out phase of this experiment. The Kaggle controller refuses a config or a listed source whose hash differs and writes heldout_deviation_record.json with the Linux identity before the first held-out trial.
user_decision_2026_11_22: After the 20 s A5 held-out (heldout_a5_kaggle, kernel notebook48a9ab731c) was analyzed and committed, the user asked for a further held-out on Kaggle with a 10 s cap that runs only two algorithms: the full A5 (C1-C4) and SEM-RRT*. In the question dialog that followed, the user chose both proposed options: fresh seeds (map 121001-121010 x planner 1216001-1216005) instead of reusing 111001-111010, and criteria 1, 2a and 3 of the 20 s registration with unchanged thresholds; 2b (J30 against A4) is dropped because A4 is not run. Proposed by Claude and taken over from the 20 s registration: one timed lane on CPU 0, validation on four cores, the same gates (smoke at 2 s, gate map seed 51001 at the 10 s cap, SEM Python/C++ bit identity) and the same 34 CTest groups.
question: On fresh maps, on one Kaggle core, with both methods stopping on their own convergence under a 10 s cap, does the primary A5 arm meet (1) correctness, (2a) the ten checks of plan 5.3 against the self-stopping C++ SEM-RRT*, and (3) speed: mean SEM-RRT* solve time / mean A5 solve time >= 5 with A5 faster in >= 90% of the pairs?

base_commit_note: HEAD when registered; the 26 sources frozen by the 20 s registration are unchanged since a445226/245f712. source_sha256 is authoritative.

methods.sem_native: SEM-RRT* project reconstruction, C++ search engine (Python/scipy native raster as preprocessing), stops on convergence by the A4 rule (as heldout_selfstop and heldout_a5_kaggle), 10 s wall-clock cap.
methods.a5_rpbit_l33_w4000: A5 primary, unchanged from heldout_a5_kaggle: A4 with C1 batch_growth (sample-counted window of 4000 samples on batches 500/500/1000/2000), C2 fast_validity (slope-envelope shortcut, decision-identical to SafetyPolicy), C3 lazy_refine and C4 seed (lattice seed refined by rpRefine, sampling bounded by the published J); lambda 33, eps 0.1%, refinement parameters of A4; 10 s cap.

convergence_stop.sem: At every iteration boundary after the first solution: stop once 4000 iterations pass without a >= 0.1% relative drop of the published native cost; otherwise the 10 s cap ends the run (termination TIME_BUDGET).
convergence_stop.a5: Same test counted in random samples (4000) at batch boundaries; batch sizes 500/500/1000/2000 after the first solution.
convergence_stop.validation: tools/rp_bit_validation.py: the A5 checks (requested/effective options, batch schedule, stop, seed event, heuristic bound) and the SEM stop checks are correctness errors.

inputs.novelty: map seeds 121001-121010 and planner seeds 1216001-1216005 appear in no earlier config, tool, test, document, log, report or result as a seed (whole work tree searched 2026-11-22 with word boundaries: 1216001-1216005 occur only in this experiment's files; 121001-121010 occur only as unrelated byte counts, edge/heuristic counters and timestamp fractions). tests/test_rp_bit_tooling.py A5TenSecondConfigTests checks every config.

timing_protocol: Kaggle CPU session (no accelerator). execution.cores [0]: one timed lane, one trial at a time, so the two methods never run concurrently.
One fresh process per trial, pinned to its lane core, one thread.
The two methods of a (map, planner seed) block run back to back on the same core; the method order rotates between blocks.
Time (judged) = solve_time_s: A5 from before potential construction to its own stop (potential, seed, BIT*, refinement); SEM-RRT* from planner construction to its own stop or the 10 s cap.

Time before the solve clock (reported, not judged) = preprocessing_s + field_build_s: input loading in the worker (for SEM-RRT* also its native raster) plus, for A5, the SEM field built before the worker (binary container). Library imports and host identification happen before these clocks, as in heldout_a5_kaggle.
Validation is not timed and runs only after the collection of a phase is complete, on execution.validation_cores [0, 1, 2, 3].
gates_before_heldout: The controller refuses to start if the config, a phase config or any file of source_sha256 differs from this registration.
Linux build of the delivered sources; the 34 CTest groups of heldout_a5_kaggle (31 of fairtime/selfstop plus rp_bit_a5_core, rp_bit_a5_worker and terrain_unit).
smoke_a5_10s: 7 smoke fixtures, 2 s, both methods; no correctness error, every A5 trial successful, strict validation.
gate_a5_10s: the 5 families at map seed 51001, planner seed 516001, 10 s cap, both methods; same conditions.

sem_cpp_bit_identity: on the 5 gate_a5_10s maps, planner seeds 516001 and 516002, Python and C++ SEM-RRT* (stop off) each run 7425 iterations and must be identical (10/10) on the Linux runtime of the campaign.
A SEM-RRT* planner failure in a gate is a result, not a gate failure; a correctness error of either method is.
Any failed gate stops the run before the held-out; the cause is reported, nothing is retuned.

primary_criteria.source: A5 plan section 3 (approved 2026-11-21) as applied by the 20 s registration (logs/a4_rpbit_a5_heldout_20261122/registration.json), thresholds unchanged; 2b is not judged because A4 is not run (user decision of 2026-11-22). All three judged on the primary arm.

tools.tools/analyze_rp_bit_a5_sem.py: a5_verdict.json / A5_VERDICT.md: applies the thresholds below

items.1_correctness: Every planned trial has a verdict; no correctness error in either method (fast validation of every trial, strict per-snapshot validation of the primary); the primary was strictly validated. A heuristic bound violation is a correctness error. The primary's PSR is reported here but not required to be 250/250: PSR is judged by psr_pooled and psr_every_family of 2a, i.e. A5 >= SEM-RRT*.
items.2a_ten_checks_vs_sem: The ten checks of plan 5.3, primary minus sem_native: psr_pooled, psr_every_family, sti_lower, time_lower, j_sem_mean_lower, j_sem_upper95_below_zero, apl_noninferior, pri_noninferior (upper 95% bound of the pooled relative difference < +1%), apl_target_lower, pri_target_lower (mean paired difference < 0); hierarchical bootstrap map -> seed, 20000 replicates, seed 61016. All ten must pass.
items.3_speed_vs_sem: On the slots where both end on a final safe path: mean sem_native solve_time_s / mean primary solve_time_s >= 5, and the primary is faster in >= 90% of those pairs. Both bounds inclusive. A SEM-RRT* run ended by the 10 s cap counts with its capped time.

not_judged.2b_j30_vs_a4: A4 is not run in this experiment.

primary_criteria.pairing: Paired metrics use the slots where both methods end with a final safe path; PSR counts every slot.
primary_criteria.verdict: The A5 claim at the 10 s cap on unseen maps holds only if all three pass. Each item is reported separately; no item is dropped, added or re-thresholded after any held-out result is seen.

secondary_descriptive: Time before the solve clock per method, and the SEM/A5 ratio with it added (pooled and per family): reported, not judged.
Termination reasons and stop times of both methods, in particular the number of SEM-RRT* runs ended by the 10 s cap; anytime table at T in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10} s.
From the raw archive: A5 seed status by family, runs whose final path is the seed, first-publication quality, time split (setup, seed, refinement).
stated_expectation: From heldout_a5_kaggle (20 s cap, seeds 111001-111010): A5 never ran longer than 2.7 s, so the 10 s cap does not change A5; 29/250 SEM-RRT* runs went past 10 s (15 mixed_obstacles, 11 rolling_terrain, 3 narrow_passage). Capping those runs at 10 s lowers SEM/A5 on the same data from 6.20 to 5.62 (A5 still faster in 249/250 pairs); per family traversable_hill 4.78 and ridge_pass 4.14 are unchanged, narrow_passage 5.16 -> 4.94, rolling_terrain 7.73 -> 6.83, mixed_obstacles 8.26 -> 6.85. The quality of SEM-RRT* at 10 s on those data equals its 20 s quality (J30 167.567 at both; A5 minus SEM at 10 s: dJ30 -0.92, upper bound -0.78; APL upper relative bound -0.38%; PRI +0.20%). Expected here: 1 passes; 3 passes but closer to the bound than at 20 s (about 5.6 if the maps behave like 111001-111010; maps with fewer long SEM runs lower it). Within 2a, pri_target_lower is the check at risk: at 20 s the pooled PRI difference was -0.03% with a 95% interval of [-0.31%, +0.26%] and A5 lower in 147/250 pairs, so its sign on fresh maps is close to a coin flip; the other nine checks had clear margins. Every outcome is reported.
rules: Started trials are never retried; no seeds are added; criteria and analysis are not changed after any held-out result is seen.
Strict per-snapshot validation of the primary method; fast independent validation of every trial (including the stop rules).
Results are reported as measured on Kaggle Linux; their Time is not compared with Windows numbers and not pooled with other held-outs.

delivery_plan: kaggle_a4_rpbit: EXPERIMENTS['a5_10s'] with this registration and the 34 CTest groups, module kaggle_a4_rpbit/a5_10s.py; the reporting step runs the verdict tool named by the experiment (tools/analyze_rp_bit_a5_sem.py here, tools/analyze_rp_bit_a5.py for a5).
Packager profile 'a5_10s' and bundle tests; Windows rehearsal of smoke and gate before delivery; delivery audit.
limitations: The 10 s cap ends some SEM-RRT* runs before they converge (29/250 on the 20 s held-out maps): their Time is the cap, which lowers SEM's mean time (against A5 in criterion 3), and their paths are not converged (for A5 in the quality checks; on the 20 s held-out maps the SEM quality at 10 s and 20 s was the same).
C3 and C4 were redesigned after seeing the dev maps; heldout_a5_kaggle was their first test on unseen maps, this is the second.
The A5 seed is A* on the SEM cell lattice plus rpRefine, not BIT*; its share of final paths is reported.
SEM-RRT* is a project reconstruction, not the authors' code.
Shared cloud VM: background load can add timing noise; the two methods of a block share the core and rotate order.
The stop window is matched in samples/iterations, not in time or work.
